children: The Toronto speech from Bank of Canada Gov. Tiff Macklem, alongside other recent BOC communications, suggest officials are "increasingly inclined" to continue raising interest rates rather than wait for evidence that higher energy prices are spilling over to other goods, says Ruchir Sharma, economist at Nomura. The firm expects a BOC hike in December, taking the central bank's policy rate to 2.75%. Sharma says that while Macklem acknowledged the recent drop in crude-oil prices, he instead placed more emphasis on the cost pressures accumulating since the spring. A better-than-expecting economy might allow companies to pass on those increased costs through higher prices, Sharma says. Sharma adds Nomura expects the BOC to hold after the policy rate reaches 2.75%, due to soft underlying conditions in the Canadian economy. (paul.vieira@wsj.com; @paulvieira)
